Divergence measures net outward flux — field lines spreading out and breaking away from a point.
Curl captures local rotation and circulation in a field — the same spinning, dizzying sense as the song's title.

A surface integral measures flux — the flow of a field current passing through a surface.
Green's theorem ties a line integral around a region's boundary to a double integral over its interior.
Stokes' theorem generalises Green's theorem to curved surfaces in three dimensions — a bigger version of the same idea.
The theorem relates what's happening inside a solid (divergence, volume) to what appears on its outer surface — the inside reflected outward.
